data_sources: EFSA Comprehensive European Food Consumption Database
EFSA Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for carbohydrates and dietary fibre (2010)
Ingredient estimation for Norwegian ready meals based on declared ingredients on packaging
_meta.notes: Compound values are 0-3 (0=negligible, 1=low, 2=medium, 3=high) per standard European serving. Ready meal compound values are estimated from declared ingredient lists. Duplicates from the original food list have been deduplicated.

compounds.raffinose: Oligosaccharides (GOS/RFO) - fermented by gut bacteria -> CO2 + H2 -> bloating
compounds.inulin_fos: Fructooligosaccharides & inulin - highly fermentable -> gas, bloat
compounds.lactose: Milk sugar - undigested in lactase-deficient people -> osmotic + fermentation
compounds.fructose: Fruit sugar - absorbed by limited GLUT-5 transporters; excess -> osmotic
compounds.sorbitol: Sugar alcohol - poorly absorbed, osmotically active, inhibits fructose uptake
compounds.mannitol: Sugar alcohol - poorly absorbed, osmotically active
compounds.xylitol: Sugar alcohol - poorly absorbed, osmotically active
compounds.resistant_starch: Starch that escapes small intestine -> colonic fermentation -> gas
compounds.soluble_fiber: Fermentable fiber (pectin, guar, beta-glucan) -> SCFA + gas production
compounds.insoluble_fiber: Less fermentable fiber; speeds transit; bulk former
compounds.sulfur_aa: Sulfur amino acids (methionine, cysteine) -> H2S + methanethiol -> smelly gas
compounds.glucosinolates: Cruciferous sulfur compounds -> H2S via bacterial metabolism -> very smelly gas
compounds.allicin_compounds: Organosulfur in alliums (garlic/onion) -> sulfide gases -> smelly gas
compounds.tryptophan: Amino acid -> bacterial conversion to indole + skatole -> fecal odor
compounds.high_protein: General high protein load -> putrefaction (cadaverine, putrescine, indole)
compounds.fat_high: High fat -> triggers large bile acid release -> secretory effect in colon
compounds.capsaicin: Chili compound -> TRPV1 activation -> accelerated motility + secretion
compounds.caffeine: Stimulates colonic motility via adenosine receptors -> loose stool
compounds.alcohol: Damages intestinal mucosa; stimulates secretion; accelerates motility
compounds.tannins: Polyphenols in tea/wine/coffee - can cause constipation or irritation
compounds.magnesium: Osmotically active ion; high intake -> osmotic diarrhea
compounds.gluten: Gliadin protein -> immune/inflammatory reaction in sensitive individuals
compounds.histamine: Biogenic amine in fermented/aged foods -> GI irritation + motility

foods.name: Beef Tenderloin (Psoas major)
foods.note: Leanest premium cut. ~3.7g fat/100g raw. Very high protein, moderate sulfur AA.

foods.name: Beef Ribeye (Longissimus thoracis)
foods.note: High intramuscular fat (marbling). ~15-20g fat/100g raw. Rich bile acid load.

foods.name: Beef Striploin (Longissimus lumborum)
foods.note: Moderate marbling. ~10g fat/100g raw.

foods.name: Beef Chuck / Shoulder (Triceps brachii / Clod)
foods.note: Working muscle with connective tissue. ~10g fat/100g raw. Common as stew/mince.

foods.name: Beef Flat Iron (Infraspinatus)
foods.note: Tender shoulder cut. ~8g fat/100g raw.

foods.name: Beef Top Sirloin (Gluteus medius)
foods.note: Lean rump cut. ~5g fat/100g raw.

foods.name: Beef Topside / Inside Round (Semimembranosus)
foods.note: Very lean round cut. ~3-5g fat/100g raw. Common as roast or thin-sliced.

foods.name: Beef Silverside / Bottom Round (Biceps femoris)
foods.note: Lean hind cut. ~4-6g fat/100g raw. Often slow-cooked or corned.

foods.name: Beef Eye of Round (Semitendinosus)
foods.note: Very lean, low marbling. ~3g fat/100g raw. Lowest fat beef muscle cut.

foods.name: Beef Brisket (Pectoralis profundus)
foods.note: High fat, collagen-dense. ~15-20g fat/100g raw. Slow-cooked. Significant bile acid trigger.

foods.name: Beef Flank (Rectus abdominis)
foods.note: Lean, coarse-grained. ~7g fat/100g raw.

foods.name: Beef Neck
foods.note: High connective tissue and fat. ~12g fat/100g raw. Often minced or braised.

foods.name: Beef Shank / Shin
foods.note: Very lean, collagen-rich. ~4g fat/100g raw. Slow-cook only.

foods.name: Beef Diaphragm / Outside Skirt
foods.note: Respiratory muscle. ~10g fat/100g raw. High myoglobin = intense flavor. Moderate sulfur AA.

foods.name: Pork Loin (Longissimus dorsi)
foods.note: Very lean pork cut (svinefilet/kotelettstykke). ~4g fat/100g raw.

foods.name: Pork Shoulder / Blade (svineskulder)
foods.note: Moderate-high fat. ~12g fat/100g raw. Common for pulled pork and mince.

foods.name: Pork Belly (svinebrystet/side)
foods.note: Very high fat. ~30-40g fat/100g raw depending on thickness. Major bile acid trigger.

foods.name: Pork Leg / Ham, fresh (svinestek/lår)
foods.note: Lean hind cut. ~7g fat/100g raw. Not cured (cured ham has higher histamine).

foods.name: Pork Neck / Collar (svinenakke)
foods.note: Well-marbled neck cut. ~15g fat/100g raw. Classic slow-cook or ramen cut.

foods.name: Pork Spare Ribs (svineribbe)
foods.note: Very high fat between ribs. ~25-30g fat/100g raw. National Norwegian dish. Significant bile acid load.

foods.name: Pork Cheek (svinnekinn)
foods.note: Rich, gelatinous facial muscle. ~12g fat/100g raw. Popular in European slow-cooking.

foods.name: Pork Knuckle / Hock, meat portion (svinekno)
foods.note: High collagen, moderate fat. ~10g fat/100g raw meat (excluding rind).

foods.name: Chicken Breast (Pectoralis major), skinless (kyllingbryst)
foods.note: Leanest common protein source. ~1-2g fat/100g raw. Very high protein.

foods.name: Chicken Thigh, skinless (kyllinglår, uten skinn)
foods.note: Higher fat than breast. ~5g fat/100g raw skinless.

foods.name: Chicken Drumstick, skinless (kyllingtrommelstikke)
foods.note: Similar to thigh. ~5g fat/100g raw skinless.

foods.name: Chicken Wing (kyllingvinge)
foods.note: Higher fat due to skin ratio. ~12g fat/100g with skin.

foods.name: Chicken Back / Oyster (kyllingrygge)
foods.note: High bone-to-meat ratio, moderate fat from proximity to carcass fat. ~10g fat/100g edible portion.

foods.name: Lamb Leg (lammestek/lår)
foods.note: Moderate fat. ~9g fat/100g raw. Strong sulfur amino acid profile typical of ruminants.

foods.name: Lamb Shoulder (lammeskulder)
foods.note: Higher fat than leg. ~15g fat/100g raw. Richer flavor, used in braises.

foods.name: Lamb Loin Chop (lammekotelett)
foods.note: Tender loin cut. ~12g fat/100g raw trimmed. Classic Norwegian grillcut.

foods.name: Beef Liver (okselever)
foods.note: Very high protein, very high tryptophan (~290mg/100g). Moderate fat. Elevated histamine due to immune/lymphatic activity and histidine pools. High magnesium.

foods.name: Beef Kidney (oksenyrer)
foods.note: High protein, lean. Elevated histamine — kidneys filter blood and concentrate bioactive amines. Distinct sulfurous odor from urea compounds.

foods.name: Beef Heart (oksehjerte)
foods.note: Densely muscular cardiac tissue. Lean (~4g fat/100g). Very high protein and CoQ10. Lower histamine than liver/kidney.

foods.name: Beef Tongue (oksetunge)
foods.note: High fat muscle. ~15g fat/100g raw. Rich collagen and fat make it one of the fattier offal cuts.

foods.name: Beef Tripe / Rumen (oksemage/innmat)
foods.note: Stomach lining, mostly collagen (very low tryptophan — collagen lacks it). Lean. Mild histamine. Moderate sulfur from stomach environment.

foods.name: Beef Lung (okselunge)
foods.note: Very lean respiratory tissue. Lower tryptophan than muscle. Mild histamine.

foods.name: Beef Spleen (oksemilt)
foods.note: Blood-filtering organ, high iron. Elevated histamine (immune organ with mast cells). Lean.

foods.name: Beef Brain (oksehjerne)
foods.note: Extremely high fat (~10g/100g mostly phospholipids and cholesterol). Very high tryptophan (~240mg/100g). Soft texture — triggers large bile acid release.

foods.name: Beef Bone Marrow (beinmarg)
foods.note: Almost pure fat (~80g fat/100g edible marrow). Negligible protein. The single strongest bile acid trigger in the list. Used as roasted marrow in Norwegian/European cuisine.

foods.name: Pork Liver (svinelever)
foods.note: Very similar profile to beef liver. Slightly higher vitamin A. ~290mg tryptophan/100g. Moderate histamine.

foods.name: Pork Kidney (svinenyrer)
foods.note: Lean, high protein. Concentrated bioactive amines from blood filtration. Strong sulfurous note.

foods.name: Pork Heart (svinehjerte)
foods.note: Dense cardiac muscle. Lean (~4g fat/100g). High protein, moderate histamine.

foods.name: Pork Stomach / Maw (svinemage)
foods.note: Similar to beef tripe. Collagen-rich, low tryptophan. Lean. Mild sulfur from gastric environment.

foods.name: Pork Tongue (svinetunge)
foods.note: Fatty muscular organ. ~14g fat/100g raw. High protein. Often cured in Norway (higher histamine if cured — value here is fresh).

foods.name: Pork Brain (svinehjerne)
foods.note: Similar to beef brain. High phospholipid fat. Very high tryptophan. Triggers bile acid secretion.

foods.name: Pork Lung (svinelunge)
foods.note: Very lean, spongy respiratory tissue. Low tryptophan. Mild histamine.

foods.name: Chicken Liver (kyllinglever)
foods.note: Excellent source of folate and iron. ~5g fat/100g. Very high tryptophan (~300mg/100g). Moderate histamine — common pate ingredient.

foods.name: Chicken Heart (kyllinghjerte)
foods.note: Very lean, small but nutrient-dense cardiac muscle. ~7g fat/100g. High protein and CoQ10.

foods.name: Chicken Gizzard (kyllingkråse)
foods.note: Muscular grinding organ (ventriculus). Very lean (~2g fat/100g). Tough texture. Low tryptophan relative to muscle — mostly collagenous connective tissue mixed with muscle.

foods.name: Lamb Liver (lammelever)
foods.note: Very similar to beef liver. High tryptophan (~280mg/100g). Higher flavor intensity than other livers. Moderate histamine.

foods.name: Lamb Kidney (lammenyrer)
foods.note: Lean filtration organ. Strong sulfurous character (higher than beef kidney due to volatile thiol compounds in lamb). Elevated histamine.
